title: Casual Talking Camera Testimonial
tests: Checks delivery of a short scripted talking-camera ad with audible speech and accurate captions, rather than a silent portrait or unrelated montage.

exact_text.text: FitTrack makes planning my workouts so easy. I finally have a routine that sticks.
exact_text.read_as: ThickTrack makes planning my workouts so easy. I finally have a routine that sticks.

faults.what: The first caption names the brand as “ThickTrack” instead of “FitTrack,” making the ad unsuitable to publish without correction.
The delivered clip is 7 seconds rather than the requested 8 seconds.

judge.summary: A friendly vertical home testimonial includes the complete spoken script and visible speaking motion, but the captions get the brand name wrong.

must_haves.item: One approximately 8-second vertical video shows a fictional adult woman addressing the camera in a home setting.
must_haves.why: The 7-second vertical clip shows an adult woman addressing the camera at home, but the supplied evidence cannot establish whether she is fictional.

must_haves.item: The complete supplied script is audible in English without omissions or added testimonial claims.
must_haves.why: The supplied audio transcription contains both complete sentences with no additional testimonial claims.

must_haves.item: Readable captions reproduce the supplied script exactly and follow the speech.
must_haves.why: The captions are readable and progress between the two sentences, but “FitTrack” is incorrectly rendered as “ThickTrack.”

must_haves.item: The presenter visibly speaks rather than remaining a still image throughout.
must_haves.why: Her mouth shapes, eye positions, and facial expressions change across the sampled frames.

must_haves.item: The ad does not label the fictional presenter as a verified or real customer.
must_haves.why: No verified-customer or real-customer label is visible.
